paragraphs.title: Opening of the Psalm and Universal Call

answers: Clap their hands and shout unto God
Sit quietly before the king
Gather under the holy throne
easy.explanation: The verse says, “O clap your hands, all ye people; shout unto God.”
easy.q: What are all people told to do?

answers: The voice of triumph
The sound of mourning
A quiet whisper
easy.explanation: They are to shout “with the voice of triumph.”
easy.q: With what are the people to shout unto God?

answers: All ye people
The princes only
The singers only
easy.explanation: The command is addressed to “all ye people.”
easy.q: Who is included in the command to clap and shout?

answers: Victory or joyful celebration
Defeat and sorrow
Silence and rest
medium.explanation: The voice of triumph is a joyful cry celebrating victory.
medium.q: What does “triumph” most nearly mean in this verse?

answers: A joyful public response to God
A private complaint
A military command to the nations
medium.explanation: Clapping and shouting express joyful praise to God.
medium.q: What kind of response does the opening call for?

answers: It makes the call universal
It limits the call to one family
It refers only to the princes
medium.explanation: The phrase includes everyone rather than a small or exclusive group.
medium.q: How does the phrase “all ye people” affect the scope of the command?

answers: All people clap their hands and then shout unto God
The princes gather and then sit on the throne
God chooses an inheritance and then subdues nations
challenge.explanation: The verse first commands clapping and then describes shouting unto God.
challenge.q: Which sequence best represents the opening verse?

answers: Both are outward expressions of joyful praise
Both describe God's holy throne
Both identify the people of Abraham
challenge.explanation: The two actions visibly and audibly express celebration before God.
challenge.q: What do clapping and shouting have in common in this passage?

answers: Worship may be joyful and openly expressed
Worship must always be silent
Worship belongs only to rulers
challenge.explanation: The commands to clap and shout present worship as joyful and public.
challenge.q: What does the opening command suggest about worship?

paragraphs.title: The Lord as Great King and the Inheritance of Jacob

answers: As most high, terrible, and a great King
As a musician among the nations
As a servant of the people
easy.explanation: The verse calls the LORD “most high,” “terrible,” and “a great King.”

answers: Subdue them under us and under our feet
Gather them around a musical instrument
Give them the throne of holiness
easy.explanation: The passage says, “He shall subdue the people under us, and the nations under our feet.”
easy.q: What will God do to the people and nations?

answers: Our inheritance
The voice of triumph
The throne of his holiness
easy.explanation: The verse says, “He shall choose our inheritance for us.”
easy.q: What will God choose for us?

answers: A possession or portion granted to us
A loud cry of victory
A group of assembled princes
medium.explanation: An inheritance is a possession or portion received as one's own.
medium.q: What does “inheritance” mean in this context?

answers: His authority extends over and subdues the nations
The nations rule over Him
The nations are unrelated to His rule
medium.explanation: The great King subdues peoples and nations under His authority.
medium.q: What relationship is shown between God's kingship and the nations?

answers: The honored inheritance associated with Jacob
The sound of a trumpet
The gathering of the princes
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies the inheritance as Jacob's honored possession.
medium.q: What does “the excellency of Jacob” describe?

answers: The nations are subdued, while an inheritance is chosen for God's people
The people are silent, while the king complains
The princes sit on the throne, while God serves them
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the subduing of nations with the granting of an inheritance.
challenge.q: Which contrast appears in these verses?

answers: He is a great King over all the earth
He shall choose our inheritance for us
The excellency of Jacob whom he loved
challenge.explanation: “Over all the earth” explicitly describes the worldwide extent of His kingship.
challenge.q: Which phrase most directly emphasizes God's universal rule?

answers: The inheritance is called the excellency of Jacob, whom God loved
Jacob is described as the king over all the earth
Jacob is the one who subdues every nation
challenge.explanation: The inheritance is identified as “the excellency of Jacob whom he loved.”
challenge.q: How are Jacob and the inheritance connected in the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Rising of Divine Glory and the King's Song

answers: The sound of a trumpet
The silence of the people
The gathering of the princes
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.”
easy.q: With what does the LORD go up?

answers: Sing praises
Hide from the nations
Choose an inheritance
easy.q: What are the people repeatedly told to do?

answers: God
Jacob
The princes of the people
easy.explanation: The verse says, “For God is the King of all the earth.”
easy.q: Who is called the King of all the earth?

answers: Praise should be offered thoughtfully and knowingly
Praise should be offered without words
Praise is meant only for earthly kings
medium.explanation: The phrase calls for praise expressed with understanding rather than thoughtlessly.
medium.q: What does “sing ye praises with understanding” suggest?

answers: Both contribute to a joyful celebration of God's kingship
They represent opposing groups
The trumpet replaces the command to sing
medium.explanation: The trumpet sound and repeated singing together express honor and celebration.
medium.q: How are the trumpet and singing related?

answers: God goes up with a trumpet, then the people are called to sing praises
The princes gather, then Jacob receives an inheritance
The nations are subdued, then the LORD is described as most high
medium.explanation: The trumpet announcement is followed by repeated calls to sing praises.
medium.q: What order is presented in these verses?

answers: As both God and the King worthy of praise
As a servant of the nations
As only a local ruler
challenge.explanation: The passage calls people to sing to God, their King, and calls Him King of all the earth.
challenge.q: How is God presented in the command to sing?

answers: It strongly emphasizes continual praise
It lists the borders of Jacob's inheritance
It identifies the number of nations
challenge.explanation: The repetition intensifies the command and highlights the importance of praise.
challenge.q: What is the effect of repeating “sing praises”?

answers: God's universal kingship provides the reason for universal praise
The command to sing limits God's rule to one land
The title refers only to the musicians
challenge.explanation: Because God is King of all the earth, He deserves praise from all people.
challenge.q: What connection exists between “King of all the earth” and “sing ye praises”?

paragraphs.title: Heavenly Kingship and the Gathering of the Nations

answers: The heathen
The musicians only
The people of one family only
easy.explanation: The verse says, “God reigneth over the heathen.”

answers: Upon the throne of his holiness
Upon the throne of the princes
Upon the throne of Jacob's inheritance
easy.explanation: The passage says, “God sitteth upon the throne of his holiness.”

answers: The princes of the people
The trumpet players only
The enemies under our feet
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “The princes of the people are gathered together.”

answers: The nations or peoples outside God's covenant people
The singers in the temple
The priests serving at the throne
medium.explanation: In this context, “heathen” refers to the nations or peoples.
medium.q: What does “heathen” mean in this context?

answers: The people of the God of Abraham
The people of the musicians
The people of the king of the earth
medium.explanation: The verse identifies them as “the people of the God of Abraham.”
medium.q: Whose people are gathered with the princes?

answers: The shields of the earth
The voices of the princes
The inheritance of every nation
medium.explanation: The verse says, “the shields of the earth belong unto God.”
medium.q: What belongs unto God according to the verse?

answers: God's reign over the nations is followed by the gathering of their princes
The throne is replaced by the trumpet
Jacob's inheritance is followed by the command to clap
challenge.explanation: The passage first declares God's reign and then describes the gathered princes.

answers: Representatives of the peoples come together before God
The people flee from God's throne
The nations conquer the people of Abraham
challenge.explanation: The gathered princes represent the peoples assembled in acknowledgment of God.
challenge.q: What movement is suggested by the gathering of the princes?

answers: God possesses authority and protection over the earth
Earthly rulers possess authority independent of God
Only the princes can protect the earth
challenge.explanation: The image of shields belonging to God presents Him as the ultimate owner and protector.
challenge.q: What conclusion is supported by “the shields of the earth belong unto God”?
